scope: One isolated, synthetic, single-host Keycloak 26.7.0 OIDC lifecycle against two production-built Next.js 16.2.12 processes using one authenticated persistent Redis 8.2.8 revocation authority. The exercise proves distinct same-subject sessions, signed session-scoped provider logout into one replica, targeted old-cookie denial through both replicas, unaffected-session admission, cross-replica replay, fail-closed Redis loss, process liveness, durable Redis restart, cutoff/replay recovery, and later-login admission. It is not protected staging, multi-host, external identity-provider, managed Redis, production ingress, alert-delivery, compliance, penetration-test, reliability-SLO, or production-readiness evidence.

identityProvider.name: Keycloak
identityProvider.mode: isolated host-process development identity provider with HTTPS enabled

redis.mode: authenticated loopback standalone server with append-only persistence, appendfsync always, and a forced pre-failure snapshot

application.runtime: two next start processes with NODE_ENV=production and NODE_OPTIONS=--throw-deprecation

isolatedTopology.data: synthetic repository identity fixture copied and modified only inside the temporary runtime
isolatedTopology.tls: ephemeral self-signed loopback certificate trusted only by the verifier, browser, and child web processes
isolatedTopology.keycloakBackchannelTransport: bounded loopback HTTP relay retaining the signed Logout Token only in process memory
isolatedTopology.redisPersistence: append-only plus explicit pre-failure snapshot in the isolated runtime directory

liveDistributedLifecycle.command: pnpm verify:live-oidc-distributed with checksum-verified runtime paths supplied through the process environment

focusedAuthenticationTests.command: pnpm exec vitest run --project unit apps/web/src/federated-logout.test.ts apps/web/src/oidc-backchannel-logout.test.ts apps/web/src/oidc-environment.test.ts apps/web/src/oidc-session.test.ts apps/web/src/server-session.test.ts apps/web/src/session-revocation.test.ts

managed Redis failover and transport/network policy

external HTTPS back-channel ingress and alert delivery

limitations: This is an isolated single-host synthetic loopback exercise, not protected staging, multi-host, external IdP, managed Redis, production ingress, compliance, penetration-test, or production-readiness evidence.

Ephemeral self-signed loopback TLS terminates in verifier-owned Node proxies; it does not prove the deployable Nginx policy or an external load balancer, CDN, certificate, collector, or network policy.

Keycloak delivered the signed Logout Token through a loopback HTTP relay that retained it only in process memory for bounded replay and outage assertions; production back-channel transport must use the exact approved HTTPS route.

The exercise covers one abrupt Redis process loss and persistent restart. It does not prove managed failover, cross-host partitions, Sentinel/Cluster behavior, alert delivery, clock boundaries, or coordinated SESSION_SECRET/provider-signing-key rotation.
No raw provider credential, browser cookie, logout token, authorization code, state, PKCE value, Redis credential/key, password, subject, or session identifier is emitted.
No database, tenant, financial, connector, source-system, or reconciliation behavior changed, and no new database or provider-sandbox result is claimed.
No file was staged, committed, pushed, published, or deployed, and no runtime .env file was created.
